arm-A.title: The Agent training program
arm-A.summary: In a city street that is revealed to be a training program rather than the Matrix, Morpheus moves through the crowd while Neo is bumped and shouldered off the path. He teaches that Agents are sentient programs who can inhabit anyone still hardwired to the system, and that every human who has fought one has died. When Agent Smith's gun appears, Neo screams in terror, then retreats into skeptical jokes. Morpheus tells him he can become stronger and faster than any Agent, because their strength and speed are bound by rules while his are not, leaving Neo half-believing the promise on authority rather than understanding it.
arm-A.action: Morpheus walks Neo through the frozen street, reclassifying the ordinary people as part of the enemy system and using the woman in the red dress to spring Agent Smith's gun on him. As Neo is jolted by involuntary terror at the gun, Morpheus explains that Agents are sentient programs inhabiting anyone still plugged in, that no one who fought one survived, but that Neo can surpass them because their power is rule-bound while his is not. Neo, who began believing he was inside the real Matrix and confused when it froze, learns this is a training program and that anyone not yet unplugged is potentially an Agent, and ends half-believing the promise that he can exceed an Agent.

His self-conception as an ordinary man lags badly behind what Morpheus and the world demand of him, and that gap is where his fear lives.

arm-B.title: The Agent training program
arm-B.summary: On a crowded downtown street that turns out to be a training program, Morpheus moves effortlessly through the jostling crowd while Neo is bumped and shouldered off the path, and reframes the ordinary people around them as the enemy. He stops the simulation around a gun-levelled Agent, leaving everything else frozen, and uses it to teach that Agents are sentient programs who can move into anyone still hardwired to the system. He tells Neo that every human who has fought one has died, but that Neo can surpass any Agent because their strength and speed are bound by rules while his are not.
arm-B.action: Morpheus walks untroubled through the crowded downtown street as Neo is constantly bumped and shouldered, then freezes the program around a gun-levelled Agent and delivers the doctrine on what Agents are and the lethal stakes of fighting them, reframing Neo's weakness as a rule-bound limit he can overcome.

state_triples.reading: Neo is trying to rebuild his picture of reality faster than his fear will let him: every answer Morpheus gives ('This isn't the Matrix?', 'What are they?', 'Someone?') is a mind catching up, and the reflexive joke about dodging bullets is a reach back toward skepticism because believing the truth is more frightening than doubting it. He trusts Morpheus on awe and authority rather than understanding, and his sense of himself as an ordinary man lags badly behind what he is being told he is — the gap that Morpheus is betting he can close.

arm-B.title: The Sentinel hunt and the ship's hiding
arm-B.summary: A routine check-in on a parallel pipeline turns into an evasion drill when a Sentinel sweeps in on the Nebuchadnezzar. Morpheus orders the ship wedged into a narrow supply line; power is killed and the E.M.P. armed, and the crew waits frozen and freezing while the machine glides over them and passes. Once it disappears, the tension breaks and the ship settles into rest.
arm-B.action: Dozer reports a Squiddy sweeping in and Morpheus orders the ship set down; the Nebuchadnezzar is wedged into a tight pipe. Morpheus hails Tank over the intercom; Tank kills the turbines, confirms power is offline and the E.M.P. armed, and grips the glowing red key. In the darkened cockpit Trinity defines the E.M.P. for Neo, Dozer clears frost from the windshield, Morpheus stops Neo from moving with a warning that the machine will hear him, and the crew watches the machine pass before it disappears. The crew then falls asleep in the hall.

arm-A.title: Cypher's disillusionment and his deal
arm-A.summary: On the Nebuchadnezzar's main deck, Cypher pours Dozer's liquor for Neo and recasts Morpheus's prophecy as a body count, telling him five before him took on an Agent and died because Morpheus got them believing. Neo takes it as caution and retreats toward the ladder, shaken rather than converted. Cypher then crosses into the Matrix to a restaurant, where he savors an impossible steak and strikes a bargain with Agent Smith: his body returned to a power plant and reinserted as someone rich, important, and forgetful, in exchange for delivering the man who holds Zion's mainframe access codes. Smith names that man as Morpheus, and Cypher's private regret settles into reconciled treason.
arm-A.action: Cypher pours two shots of Dozer's liquor for Neo on the main deck and reframes 'save the world' as a mindjob, revealing that five candidates before Neo confronted an Agent and died because Morpheus got them believing in bullshit. Neo drinks, reddens, and takes the warning to heart as caution, then turns for the ladder, leaving Cypher at the screens. Cypher meets Agent Smith in an upscale restaurant inside the Matrix, eats a steak he knows is not real, and lays out his terms: his body carried back to a power plant and reinserted into the Matrix as someone rich and important who remembers nothing. Smith presses only for commitment, then names the deliverable man as Morpheus, the one who carries the Zion mainframe access codes.

arm-B.title: Cypher's disillusionment and his deal
arm-B.summary: Two scenes, one turn. On the Nebuchadnezzar's main deck, Cypher plays the easy veteran for Neo and uses the drink to sour him on Morpheus, confessing his own regret and reframing the prophecy as a repeating body count. He then meets Agent Smith in an upscale restaurant and, no longer conflicted, barters Morpheus for reinsertion into a rich, forgetful life inside the Matrix. The private grumbling of the cockpit becomes an open, named transaction.
arm-B.action: Alone at the operator's chair on the main deck, Cypher is startled by Neo, then pours him Dozer's engine liquor and toasts that he wishes he'd taken the blue pill. He steers the talk to why Neo is here, mocks the 'save the world' mandate as a mindjob, and reveals that Morpheus has already 'found the One' five times before — all of them dead, killed after Morpheus got them believing and each took on an Agent. He tells Neo to run from any Agent, then lets Neo leave for the ladder. Later, in an upscale restaurant, Cypher savors a steak he admits is not real and declares ignorance bliss. He lays out his price to Agent Smith: no memory of his real life, and reinsertion as someone rich and important like an actor. In return he offers his body back to a power plant and whatever Smith wants; Smith names the access codes to the Zion mainframe, and when Cypher says he can't supply them, Smith names the man who can — Morpheus.

arm-A.title: Entering the building and meeting the Oracle
arm-A.summary: The crew arrives at a vast, tenement-like building and, as they move through it, it is revealed as a place where people can disappear. Morpheus and Neo go up in the elevator and down a dark hall to a door Neo resists; there Morpheus confesses that he misread the Oracle, thought the prophecy was about himself, and lost his way after five dead candidates, so that when the door opens on its own he has only hard-won faith to offer. Inside, the Priestess separates them—Morpheus is left waiting while a boy teaches Neo that there is no spoon, and Neo, having begun to see the spoon and the room bend, is called forward to be seen by the Oracle.
arm-A.action: The crew enters the building and ascends; Neo and Morpheus ride the elevator alone, then walk the hall to the Oracle's door, which opens for Neo before he touches it. The Priestess leads Neo into the apartment, separates him from Morpheus, and calls him to be seen, while a boy teaches him that bending the spoon is impossible because there is no spoon.

arm-B.title: Entering the building and meeting the Oracle
arm-B.summary: The party arrives at a vast tenement-like building understood as a place where people can disappear. Morpheus leads Neo up through it, into the elevator, down the hall, and to the Oracle's apartment door, while Neo follows and, at the threshold, backs away before committing. During the ascent, Neo presses Morpheus over the five failed candidates, and Morpheus confesses that he misunderstood the Oracle — that he had believed the prophecy was all about him and that he could anoint whoever he chose — admitting he was terribly wrong. He shifts from describing the Oracle in the abstract to disclosing that she personally told him he would find the One, and asks Neo to lean on residual respect and trust him until Neo can feel what he feels. Neo learns the Oracle is a fallible-sounding guide who knows enough rather than everything, and, among the Potentials, accepts the Spoon Boy's lesson that bending the spoon is impossible because there is no spoon — only oneself bends, the truth that reality here is a projection of the self, confirmed as he stares into the spoon and the reflected room slowly begins to bend. The Priestess opens the door before Neo touches it, greets him by name, and shepherds him through the household to the Oracle. Neo steps through the door into the Oracle's apartment, called forward to meet her while Morpheus is left behind, suspended between the terror of being the One and the safety of being a nobody.

arm-A.title: The Trap Springs
arm-A.summary: Fresh from the Oracle's verdict, Neo is carried back to the crew with a secret he is told to keep and a death-prophecy he cannot yet act on. The return to the Hotel Lafayette turns that prophecy physical: a repeated cat, a helicopter that should not be growing louder, and Tank's realization on the main deck that the world has been edited into an ambush. The Matrix is rewritten against them — a hardline severed, windows bricked into walls — and Mouse is cornered and killed while the rest of the crew finds every exit sealed. With the stairwell swarming below and no way out, Morpheus seizes Trinity's traceable phone despite the risk and orders Tank to find a way through the building, converting a closing trap into the first move of an escape.
arm-A.action: The crew leaves the Oracle's apartment and is carried by car to the Hotel Lafayette, then moves up the dark stairwell toward the eighth floor. A repeated cat and a helicopter growing louder than it should trigger the crew's recognition that the Matrix has been changed. On the main deck, Tank reads the edit on his screens and races to warn Mouse, but the hardline has already been cut and the windows of ROOM 1313 are bricked up; Mouse is pinned against the brick by gunfire and killed, his body flatlining. With the stairwell swarming below and every exit gone, Morpheus overrides Trinity's warning, rips off his jacket, and seizes her traceable phone as the one remaining variable, then orders Tank to find a structural drawing of the building fast.

The others are the crew's collective body temperature: unalarmed one moment, frozen the next at two words — 'deja vu.' They do not think or decide; they react as one, which is how the event marks the shift from a routine extraction to a trap. Their freeze is the visible proof that everyone but Neo and Cypher still believes the world is stable — and that the moment they stop trusting it, the hunt is on.
